llms.body:
# Fastmail

> Fastmail is an email, calendar, and contacts service paid for by its
> customers, not by advertisers, so it shows no ads and never mines customer
> data or uses it for advertising.  It's an independent email provider and has
> been in operation since 1999.  Fastmail led the design of JMAP (RFC 8620),
> the modern standard for email sync, and built the first implementation, in
> the open source Cyrus IMAP server.

Fastmail is headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, with an office in
Philadelphia, USA.  It hosts email for individuals, families, and
businesses, including on customers' own domains.  All mail, calendars, and
contacts can be reached over open standards (JMAP, IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV,
CardDAV, and WebDAV), so customers can use whatever apps they like, and can
take their data elsewhere whenever they like.

## About Fastmail

- [Fastmail home page](https://www.fastmail.com/): An overview of Fastmail's email, calendar, and contacts service
- [Pricing](https://www.fastmail.com/pricing/): The available plans, what each includes, and what each costs; Fastmail has a 30 day free trial but no free plans
- [Fastmail for business](https://www.fastmail.com/business/): Email and calendars for organizations
- [Product tour](https://www.fastmail.com/features/): A guided tour of Fastmail's features
- [About us](https://www.fastmail.com/company/about/): The company and the people behind it

## Features

- [App](https://www.fastmail.com/features/app/): Fastmail's mobile apps offer nearly every feature of the web app, including rules and settings, work offline, and can notify you only about mail from VIPs.
- [Calendar](https://www.fastmail.com/features/calendar/): Calendars built into Fastmail, with shared calendars for teams, calendars from Google, iCloud, and elsewhere shown alongside your own, time zone support, and a summary of exactly what changed when an invitation is updated.
- [Contacts](https://www.fastmail.com/features/contacts/): An address book that shows each contact's recent messages and upcoming meetings, with private notes on contacts and a shared address book for families and teams alongside a personal one.
- [Declutter your inbox](https://www.fastmail.com/features/declutter/): Spam filtering that trains a personal filter from what you report, one-click unsubscribe from mailing lists, sender blocking, and a rules engine that also accepts hand-written Sieve scripts.
- [Domains](https://www.fastmail.com/features/domains/): Email at your own domain, with a setup wizard, multiple users each with their own login, free aliases that deliver to one or more people or to an outside address, catch-all addresses, and up to 100 domains per account.
- [Lightning quick](https://www.fastmail.com/features/lightning-quick/): Why Fastmail is fast: custom servers with NVMe storage, our purpose-built mail server with multi-layer caching and full-text indexes, and preloading and optimistic updates in Fastmail's own apps.
- [Masked email](https://www.fastmail.com/features/masked-email/): Masked Email gives you a unique random address for each site you sign up with, so companies can't link your accounts to track you, and you can turn off any address that starts getting spam.  Works with 1Password, Bitwarden, and more via a published API.
- [Memos](https://www.fastmail.com/features/memos/): Private notes attached to a message, visible only to you and searchable.  Other mail apps see them as recipient-less replies in a Memos folder.
- [Migrate in minutes](https://www.fastmail.com/features/migrate/): Import mail, contacts, and calendars from any provider that supports IMAP, CardDAV, and CalDAV, including Gmail, Yahoo, and AOL, and keep fetching new mail from the old account while you switch.  No IMAP?  No problem, Fastmail can also import mbox, ics, and vcf files.
- [Mute conversations](https://www.fastmail.com/features/mute/): Muting a conversation keeps its future replies out of your inbox.  They stay searchable, and rules can act on muted conversations.
- [Pin messages](https://www.fastmail.com/features/pin/): Pinned messages stay at the top of the inbox or any other folder until unpinned, and can be found with the search `is:pinned`.  Other mail apps see pins as flags.
- [Private, naturally](https://www.fastmail.com/features/privacy/): How Fastmail protects privacy: remote images are fetched anonymously so senders can't learn your location or device, Masked Email prevents cross-site tracking, staff access to data requires a stated justification, and only valid Australian legal requests are answered.
- [Rock-solid reliability](https://www.fastmail.com/features/reliability/): How Fastmail keeps mail available and safe: real-time replication to geographically separate data centers, daily checksummed backups, redundant failover, round-the-clock monitoring, and a public status history.
- [Scheduled send](https://www.fastmail.com/features/scheduled-send/): Write a message now and have it sent at a chosen time.  It can be cancelled until then, and recipients can't tell it was scheduled.
- [Search](https://www.fastmail.com/features/search/): Full-text search, including inside attachments, with Gmail-compatible syntax, the ability to exclude senders or folders, saved searches, and bulk actions or rules on the results.
- [Security with substance](https://www.fastmail.com/features/security/): Encryption in transit (TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy) and at rest, a choice of EU or US data residency, two-step verification, passkeys, HSTS, and a strict Content Security Policy.  Fastmail's own apps deliberately don't offer end-to-end encryption; PGP and S/MIME work in third-party apps.
- [Snooze](https://www.fastmail.com/features/snooze/): Snoozing removes a message from the inbox and brings it back at a chosen time.  It only works in Fastmail's own apps, because no standard protocol supports it.
- [Make it yours](https://www.fastmail.com/features/customize/): Light and dark modes (with dark mode applied to messages too), custom colour themes, configurable swipe actions, a reading pane, plain-text reading and writing, and a choice of conversations or single messages and folders or labels.
- [Undo Everything](https://www.fastmail.com/features/undo-everything/): Undo for almost any action in mail, calendars, and contacts, plus restore from backup for permanently deleted mail (up to a week later) and for changes to contacts, calendars, and notes.
- [Undo send](https://www.fastmail.com/features/undo-send/): Sent mail is held on Fastmail's servers for 20 seconds so it can be recalled, even if you close your laptop in the meantime.  The delay can be turned off.
- [Download the app](https://www.fastmail.com/download/): Fastmail apps for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux
- [AI assistants (MCP)](https://www.fastmail.com/blog/an-mcp-server-for-fastmail/): Fastmail's official MCP server -- reachable by agents at https://api.fastmail.com/mcp -- lets AI clients work with your mail, calendars, contacts, and notes.  Users can grant varying levels of permission to each agent.  Fastmail has no AI in its own apps and does not use customer mail to train models.

## Our values

- [Our values](https://www.fastmail.com/company/values/): The principles Fastmail is run by, starting with "you are our customer, not our product"
- [Open source and standards](https://www.fastmail.com/company/open-source/): The open source projects and open standards Fastmail builds, sponsors, and contributes to
- [Data transparency report](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/transparency-report/): The requests for customer data Fastmail has received from authorities, and how it responded

## Switching to Fastmail

- [Moving from Gmail](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/move-from-gmail/): How Fastmail compares to Gmail, and how to switch
- [Moving from Outlook](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/move-from-outlook/): How Fastmail compares to Outlook, and how to switch
- [Moving from Proton Mail](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/move-from-proton/): How Fastmail compares to Proton Mail, and how to switch
- [Moving from Yahoo Mail](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/move-from-yahoo/): How Fastmail compares to Yahoo Mail, and how to switch
- [Moving from Hey](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/move-from-hey/): How Fastmail compares to Hey, and how to switch
- [Email for your own domain](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/email-for-your-domain/): How to use your own domain name for email with Fastmail
- [How to stop spam](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/stop-spam/): Practical advice on reducing spam
- [How to achieve inbox zero](https://www.fastmail.com/how-to/inbox-zero/): Practical advice on keeping an empty inbox

## Support

- [Fastmail help center](https://fastmail.help/): Documentation for every part of Fastmail, including setup guides and troubleshooting
- [Contact Fastmail support](https://www.fastmail.com/support/): How to reach Fastmail's support team
- [System status](https://fastmailstatus.com/): The current status of Fastmail's services, and any ongoing incidents
- [Report a security issue](https://www.fastmail.com/bug-bounty/): How to report a security vulnerability in Fastmail

## Developers

- [API documentation](https://www.fastmail.com/dev/): How to access Fastmail data with JMAP, IMAP, POP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV, and WebDAV, including authentication with OAuth or API tokens
- [JMAP](https://jmap.io/): The open standard for syncing email, contacts, and calendars, whose design Fastmail led, and which Fastmail's own apps use
- [API Terms of Service](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/api-terms-of-service/): Terms for using the Fastmail API
- [API Developer Policy](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/api-developer-policy/): Requirements for applications that use the Fastmail API

## Policies

- [Fastmail policies](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/): An index of all Fastmail's terms and policies
- [Terms of Service](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/terms-of-service/): The terms under which Fastmail provides its service
- [Privacy policy](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/privacy/): What data Fastmail collects, and how it is used and protected
- [Data Protection Agreement](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/dpa/): Fastmail's data processing terms, including for GDPR compliance
- [Cookies policy](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/cookies-policy/): How Fastmail's websites use cookies

## Optional

- [Fastmail blog](https://www.fastmail.com/blog/): Product announcements, company news, and technical articles
- [Digital Citizen podcast](https://www.fastmail.com/digitalcitizen/): Fastmail's podcast about privacy, open standards, and life online
- [Media kit](https://www.fastmail.com/media-kit/): Official Fastmail logos and brand guidelines
- [Sitemap](https://www.fastmail.com/sitemap.md): A complete list of pages on this site

Choose your primary data residency: EU or USA. Learn more

Email and calendar
made better

Fast, private email hosting for you or your business.

Try free for 30 days

For business

No obligation, no credit card required.

“I have used Fastmail for years and never had one problem. Not one.”

“I migrated from Google Workspace to Fastmail and would never go back.”

“I've been using Fastmail for more than ten years. I couldn't be happier.”

Better for staying on top of it all

See how much better email and calendars can be when it’s super fast, has great search, and surfaces the information you need, right when you need it.

Boost your productivity

  • Pin important messages to the top of your inbox for instant access.
  • Find any message in seconds with our powerful search.
  • Snooze tickets and bills to just when you need them.
  • Stay productive offline — read, draft, search, and manage mail, calendar, and contacts.

Protect your privacy

  • Keep your real email address private with Masked Email.
  • Use aliases to keep your side hustles separate.
  • Stop spy pixels tracking your location.

Get organized

  • Stay on schedule with our fast, beautiful calendar.
  • Know exactly what’s changed when someone updates an event.
  • See all your events in one place by adding your Google or iCloud calendars.

Stay focused

  • Elegant native apps for every platform.
  • Avoid unwanted interruptions with VIP-only notifications.
  • Work on your time with scheduled send.
  • Add private memos to messages such as reminders, payment dates, or notes.

Better isn’t easy to describe, but you know it when you see it

Best alternative to Gmail and iCloud for email, calendars, and contacts!

Jon Henshaw

Founder of Coywolf

I have used Fastmail for years and found them consistently excellent.

Dylan Beattie

Creator of the Rockstar programming language

Fastmail rocks! It’s secure, private, independent, and has a Gmail transfer tool. You won’t regret the move.

Vicky Brasseur

Open source expert and author

Better for your peace of mind

Private

Free email isn’t really free: you’re paying with your privacy. As a paid service, we only serve you, our customer. This means we have no split loyalties, no mining of your personal data, no sharing it with third parties, and no ads, ever.

See plans

Secure

Your email unlocks access to everything you do on the web. It’s the history of where you’ve been, what you buy, and who you know. We take great measures to keep it secure, backed up, and always available to you — and no one else.

Learn about email security

Personal support

From “how do I get started” to “I’ve lost my phone” panic, when you need that extra helping hand, we’re here for you. Our support team are online 24/7, providing personal support to ensure your email runs smoothly.

Get support

No lock-in

We’ve been delivering a better service for over 20 years, growing all that time — because once you’ve tried it, you won’t settle for anything else. People stay because we’re the best, not because it’s too hard to get your data out. After all, it’s your data, not ours.

Read our values

Better for everyone

We won’t let email become just another closed messaging service owned by big tech.

We don’t just make a better email service. We also make email better for everyone with our work advancing open standards and leading industry co-operation. We employ the top experts on email and calendaring, working on everything from email authentication to calendar interoperability.

Our contributions include the development of JMAP, the next-generation open sync protocol, and a wide range of open-source code used by organizations around the world. Our work keeps the internet open, and stops email becoming just another walled garden.

Read about open source and standards
